It was late and we weren't in the mood to call and wait for someone come and do their job at 10pm; we brought a can of Lysol and sprayed the pillows, sheets, and headboard liberally. We ARE in a COVID pandemic and most hotels are adhering to strict cleaning protocols however the Lemon Tree doesn't appear to be performing even basic cleaning and laundering between guests.

The headboard and dresser also had smears on them (hopefully not any sort of bodily fluid) and it looked like housekeeping made an attempt to wipe them down but didn't do a good job.

Travelocity and Hotwire both state there's a 72 hour gap between guests at the Lemon Tree (COVID protocol) but this, of course cannot be true since the room was being "cleaned" when we arrived early.

I've traveled extensively in Asia and abroad and am far from picky but this room was simply gross and more importantly, COVID protocols are not being following as simple laundering isn't happening between guests which becomes a serious safety issue.

The property is surrounded by lemon trees as soon as you walk inside to check in there was a lovely aroma of grilled garlic butter! The rooms are clean and contemporary with blow dryer in room safe microwave refrigerator toiletries if you forgot yours tourist magazines balcony or patios and seating . OK rooms are all non-smoking or you will be charged I believe $100 fine / they also place a temporary $150 cleaning fee but it's released upon check out.  One of the only places I like to stay when I go to Santa Barbara. Also Lyft drivers are also familiar with the property if you need transportation .

Don't let the lobby fool you, rooms were horrible, bed uncomfortable, it looked like it was another establishment and turned into a hotel/motel. There was a portable toilet in the bathroom it was creepy.

response:
Loquita is a trendy and classy Spanish tapas bar located in Santa Barbara, CA at 202 State St. They specialize in a variety of services including event planning, nightlife, modern European cuisine, seafood, and cocktail bars. With a high rating of 4.5 stars, customers praise the ambience, especially the romantic setting and outdoor seating. The restaurant is open from Tuesday to Sunday, 5-9pm on weekdays and until 10pm on Fridays and Saturdays. Street parking and valet services are available. 

Customers appreciate the warm outdoor dining experience and the variety of tapas offered. Favorites include the Jamon tasting, manchego tasting plate, pulpo, churros, and paella. The sangria also receives positive reviews. However, some dishes like the El bulli, patatas bravas, and Crudo have received mixed reviews. The restaurant does not offer wifi or live music. It is suitable for group outings but it is not clear if take-out service is available.

review_info.review_text: Came to loquita for the first time in SB. It's a very nice Spanish tapas restaurant with and outdoor patio and lots of fireplaces and heaters to keep guests warm at night. We ordered the el bulli, baya de oro and datil as small bites to start off the night. My favorite was the datil and the el bulli was an interesting citrus caviar but I didn't think it was mind blowing. Don't skip out on the Jamon tasting and manchego! The jamon tasting is perfect for 2 people and comes with plenty of meat (iberico, Serrano, and chorizo and pan con tomate). The manchego tasting plate was amazing and came with the best accompaniments! The almonds were out of this world and was cooked with a lavender type glaze on them which paired well with the cheese. Also, try the pulpo and churros to round off your meal. The pulpo was super tender and crisp and the churros were plenty to share. I even got to take the leftovers home for snacking later. Don't get the patatas bravas! I thought it was going to be more like a hash brown from previous photos but we got more smashed potatoes covered in like a hot mayo sauce! Definitely could have skipped on that one. Overall, it's a great dinner spot and was enjoyable on a Sunday night out.

Was a nice atmosphere. Appreciated the outdoor dining and they are very thoughtful about having ample heaters to make sure diners are warm. 

Staff was nice. 

Food was slightly disappointing:

El bulli: felt like simple tangerine pulp with a micro basil leaf
Crudo: seafood is my jam and brininess is delish but the fish in this Crudo tasted fishy and felt like a coarse hunk of fish that wasn't cured at all in acid
Pollo paella: wasn't bad but wasn't something to write home about
Churros: batter seemed very good but was burned with burnt flavor
Basque cheesecake: delicious! Light and not too sweet

This place has the best food! I thought I knew a good paella until I came here. A bit on the pricey side but well worth it. We shared it with some sangria. The sangria was perfect, but too sweet or too tart. The service was quick and simple. We'd definitely come back here the next time we're in the area.

response:
Loquita is a local business located on 202 State St in Santa Barbara, CA. It is an event planning and services establishment that also offers a vibrant nightlife experience. Loquita specializes in tapas bars, serving Spanish and modern European cuisine. The venue includes a spacious outdoor patio with fireplaces and heaters, ensuring a warm and cozy atmosphere for guests. 

Customers have praised Loquita for its diverse menu and flavorful dishes. Some recommended small bites include the el bulli, baya de oro, and datil, with the datil being a particular favorite. The Jamon tasting, featuring a variety of meats like iberico, Serrano, and chorizo, along with the manchego tasting plate, have also received rave reviews. Accompaniments like lavender-glazed almonds perfectly complement the cheese. Other standout menu items include the tender and crisp pulpo (octopus) and the churros for dessert.

While the food at Loquita generally receives positive feedback, some customers found a few dishes slightly disappointing. The el bulli was described as simple tangerine pulp with a micro basil leaf, and the Crudo felt like a coarse hunk of fish that lacked proper curing in acid. However, the Basque cheesecake was a crowd-pleaser, being described as light and not overly sweet.

Overall, Loquita offers a great dining experience, particularly for those seeking a Spanish tapas restaurant with an outdoor seating option. The ambiance has a trendy and classy feel, making it a popular spot for a Sunday night out. The business has received an average star rating of 4.5, indicating its positive reputation among customers.

The restaurant is open most days of the week, with varying hours. IHOP offers several amenities such as free WiFi, good for groups, and take-out service. Their ambience is casual and they provide parking lot facilities. However, they do not offer outdoor seating, music, or valet services. review_info.review_text: Mmm I gave into my cravings once again and visited IHOP tonight. I had been thinking about the Harvest Grain Pancakes and they did not disappoint. The service was also wonderful (I was nervous reading all of the negative reviews about the service). The plate was delivered in a timely manner and the pancakes were nice and hot. Thank you for the nostalgic experience!

This place is very hidden, and nothing too exciting but I got a birthday stack of pancakes so we went in to redeem them. The pancakes had the familiar IHOP taste, and yes they were good. Surprisingly they actually looked pretty like the staged pictures on the menu, so that's impressive. Nothing to complain about regarding the pancakes.
The service was friendly and kind, but it took a while for us to be welcomed upon entering. The place was dead when we walked in and no waiters were around. Then we didn't get checked on during our meal.
It's actually a pretty spacious interior and I could see it being quite the family place on Sunday. The only other people that were there with us were ordering off the senior menu. That seems to be the crowd here.

Never again!! The waiter (in his late 50's) who took our order seemed very irritated that we were even there from the start. Coffee tasted sour and was undrinkable, when I politely asked the irritated waiter for a new coffee, that most likely sealed our fate. Our food never arrived. We noticed two groups of people who got there 20 minutes after we did receive their food which at that point it was 45minutes since we were seated so we asked our waiter for the status of our order, he didn't say one word just nodded his head and walked away. At this point I was about to get up and and leave but my gf and sister convinced me to wait. After another 25 minutes and 3 attempts to wave our waiter down (as he kept avoiding looking our way) we all decided to get up and leave. Boycotting this business from here on and you better believe im spreading the word. 0 out of 5 stars!!!

I've often read that food prepared with love infuses that love into what you are eating. I never believed that until eating here. The food is fantastic. There are my favorites, from their Mamma Maca smoothie to the delicious Pesto Panini. Their fresh juices are unparalleled, clean in their taste and flavor combinations. And then there's the daily flavor of banana bread.  The other day I was there when the chef brought out a whole raw apple pie specially ordered for someone's Thanksgiving. She was glowing with pride for her creation, and the care the other women took in boxing it up was a sight to see. It wasn't just a pie, but rather something made special for someone's holiday.

I am vegan so I especially appreciate their vegan offerings. Their menu is organic, gluten-free, and locally sourced. You can really feel and taste the difference between food created at a chain by exhausted workers with cheaply-sourced, chemically-laden products, and food created by people with an exuberance for what they are doing and care in picking the perfect fresh ingredients for it. This should be a model for the world over.

Wonderful team and fabulous food. Their smoothies are to die for. The matcha lattee wow!!! Always smiling and helpful. My kids favorite place in Santa Barbara. I wish they would open another in Goleta.

review_info.review_text:
We ordered a bunch of food to go.  I got a green sauce chicken enchilada, crispy taco and ceasar salad.  It would definitely be better there, fresh.  The taco shell turned back into a doughy mess.  However, the taco filling was delicious.  The chicken enchilada was filled with pollo asada and it was tender and tasty.  The salad left a lot to be desired; way too much dressing and soggy lettuce.  I was wishing I had gotten beans and rice however, I was completely full with the inside of the taco and most of the enchilada, so beans and rice would have gone to waste anyway.  I will try it again and I will keep in mind the to go
aspect.
Food is good, space is beautiful, service is snotty, not sure why! I understand why they fall short of 4 Stars. :(

Despite a very kind, prompt waiter, this was one of the worst dining experiences I've ever had. The tap water tasted absolutely foul, as did the chicken and vegetable soup, so I wonder if it's because they use the tap water in the broth. The soup tasted like pure chemicals - something between chlorine and citric acid. 

Also, I am unable to eat cilantro, and our waiter kindly checked with the chef if there was any cilantro in the soup, and he was told there was not. The cilantro in the soup was clearly visible when it arrived, and the waiter apologized profusely and said he'd speak with the chef. He then told us that the chef adamantly denied using any cilantro in the dish when it was sitting right there in front of me.

I feel badly for the great wait staff, because the kitchen is absolutely offensive.

review_info.review_text:
I got a tofu banh mi, and it was pretty disappointing. The sandwich was fairly small for the price, and the inside of the sandwich was basically empty. Like, if you looked at it from the side, you would think it was just a piece of bread sliced down the middle. Seriously!

To add insult to injury, it tastes *nothing* like a banh mi. They should just call it something else because there was nothing inside that sandwich that tasted anything remotely like a banh mi does.

Three stars because my friend got a turkey sandwich that they really loved, so just averaging out the stars between the two of us.
This place slaps! I've lived in SB for 5 years and I hit Blue owls all the time. 10/10 would recommend. Fav is the Rice with pork and spicy chili sauce!

What a great little lunch spot! We dropped by one afternoon and were really pleasantly surprised but the quality of the food. Reasonably priced as well, if you factor in the Santa Barbara "tax". I got a tofu banh mi, and it was pretty disappointing. The sandwich was fairly small for the price, and the inside of the sandwich was basically empty. Like, if you looked at it from the side, you would think it was just a piece of bread sliced down the middle. Seriously!

To add insult to injury, it tastes *nothing* like a banh mi. They should just call it something else because there was nothing inside that sandwich that tasted anything remotely like a banh mi does.

Three stars because my friend got a turkey sandwich that they really loved, so just averaging out the stars between the two of us.
This place slaps! I've lived in SB for 5 years and I hit Blue owls all the time. 10/10 would recommend. Fav is the Rice with pork and spicy chili sauce!

review_info.review_text:
Love this place.  The mixologists are genius, and have great off menu suggestions (like a vodka shot with muddled fresh strawberries). The food is very fresh and locally sourced. Over three days (we stayed at the adjacent Hotel Indigo) we had the mussels in madras curry broth (amazing), the pork chop with polenta, the heirloom tomato salad, and the focaccia. We also had the goat cheese frittata for breakfast and almond brioche.
The place has a hip crowd and modern decor.

My husband and I had the opportunity to try this place out the day before New Year's Eve. We decided to stop by and sit at the bar as we were exploring the area. 

First and foremost, they have the best cocktails. The bartender was amazing and was able to hold down the fort despite a fully packed bar and restaurant. I had the bartender's special made with Vodka. It was combination of spicy and sour. My second drink was the What The French Toast. This drink was garnished with a Cinnamon Toast Crunch and tasted like the best liquid cinnamon roll I have ever had. The bartender is truly a mixologist!

We had the Wood Fired Focaccia. This was crispy on the outside and nice and doughie/fluffy on the inside. It also had a little spicy kick to it. It was truly tasty. 

The only reason this place did not receive 5 stars is because we ordered the mussels and the crab risotto and we were informed that they were out of ingredients for both dishes. That was a complete let down as the focaccia and drinks left us wanting more.
This is a must see!  It is an absolute gem to the community and the food couldn't get any better in my opinion!

source_info.name: Mama Lu
source_info.categories: Asian Fusion, Chinese, Restaurants

review_info.review_text:
I wanted to give this restaurant a try and I wasn't disappointed. The server greeted me and asked if I wanted to select the buffet as an option or a la carte. A la carte was my choice and I ordered something familiar "sweet an sour chicken" which wouldn't disappoint me. 

The arrival time of my order was approx. 12 minutes. I was served with a pot of rice and a plenty of sweet and sour chicken that I could not finish the dish even though I tried my hardest lol.

What I most appreciated about the staff was their composure and time they had given me to enjoy my meal without the extra "are you finished" and the constant hovering near my dining table. I like their relaxed demeanor.

Stopped by for a hunting trip. This restaurant hosting a buffet and a regular order restaurant. When first entered , we see greeted by a kitchen worker. Then the owner came out and served us. We ordered about 7 plates. No pictures. 

1. Taste: all the food we ordered were just standard Chinese good and does not required any sophisticated skill. All the food we ordered tastes way way way lower than all other restaurants. Trufully my 2 year old son cooks much much better than this. 0 star
2. Service:after the initial encounter with the kitchen worker then the service started receiving some service. 2star
3. Hygiene: this is considered pretty clean and neat restaurant. 4 star
4. Quality: kind of bad. The chicken we ordered were too old and dried. The soup, we're just MSG water and some fish balls in it. The water were tape water.  The tomato fried eggs( eggs over cooked tomato too raw). 1 star

BUFFET ONLY REVIEW 
Food was dry and flavorless , barely any options . Tasted worse than most take out Chinese places. You could taste how old the food was it looked like it was sitting out for about three to four hours. No ice cream or any decent deserts either besides jello. DO NOT EAT AT THE BUFFET.

review_info.review_text:
I can't believe I'm writing a review about a national chain sandwich shop, but good grief... 

I made an online order at 10:30am for a noon pickup, (2 sandwiches and a kids meal,) I showed up at noon, and they literally hadn't even started them?!  There was not a single customer in the shop and 4 employees, wondering around like chickens with their heads cut off? 

I told them to immediately get going on my sandwiches, and then once they finally began, it was llike watching paint dry. They took SO INSANELY LONG to make 3 small sandwiches. I've never seen anything like it!?  My 7 yr. old son could shuck a dozen oysters in less time...

Management needs to either start cracking the whip on these clowns or, just fire them and start over. 

Unreal!!!

Hubby and I stopped in here to get sandwiches a couple weekends ago.  First thing I noticed was that while no customers were in the store, the employee who was preparing things in the back was wearing his mask over one ear but not over his nose/mouth.  I could see this as I walked in.  The employee didn't notice us right away so I just watched.  Eventually they saw us and put their mask on properly and came over.  Our sandwiches were made correctly and quickly.  Jersey Mike's doesn't put very much meat on the default sandwich though so I recommend ordering double meat.  Everything was tasty and fresh.  Store was clean and easy to find just off the 101.  Down one star for questionable mask-wearing while no customers present.

First of all the two young teenage guys that were working we're very polite but when it comes to making sandwiches or food in general it didn't come out so good.
I got the number 55 the Big Kahuna chicken and I got the biggest size sandwich they had and then I also purchased a sandwich for later.
The Big Kahuna chicken was so nasty the chicken was overcooked, it was chewy and dry, when I opened the package to eat the sandwich it was soaking wet with what I'm assuming was the cheese? maybe??
Needless to say I ended up throwing it away that was an expensive sandwich to throw away but it was unedible.
I then tried to eat the sandwich that I had gotten  for later and it was soaking wet there was no reason why it should have been soaking wet.
I didn't get anything on it  to make it soaking wet no sauce  or any of that.
The bread was so soggy and it was only a matter of an hour prior to me opening  it that I had purchased it.
I had purchased a small sandwich for right then it was tuna I had asked how fresh the tuna was I wanted to see what it look like he grabbed the container ran back in the back and disappeared for a while then came back out and showed me the tuna and when I looked at it I could see he had made fresh tuna and put it on top of the existing I watched him put the fresher tuna on my sandwich but how fresh was that tuna I have no idea because it made me sick.
I know it was bad because I was nauseous for several hours before the tuna finally came back up.
My stomach didn't even digest the tuna which is a good sign that the food was bad when your stomach will not digest it, it knows better.
So I was only able to eat the little tiny sandwich which was the tuna and it tasted good at the time I ate it.
Later when I tried to eat my other sandwich before I was nauseous from the tuna, it was just disgusting I threw it away then I tried to eat my other sandwich that was supposed to be for later it was all soggy it was disgusting also.
I threw it away also and it was probably a good thing because if the tuna was bad God only knows how bad the other was needless to say I paid about $90 for all of our sandwiches and they didn't even come close to being as good as they looked when they were making them.
When they were making them they looked really good but this is one time looks can be very deceiving!
The only reason I'm writing this review is so that I hope nobody else gets sick first of all, and second of all they don't waste their money.
I had also left a 10% tip on our order.
All I have to say is eat cautiously if you eat here
If this was the first time I had ever had Jersey Mike's I would never go back.
Sorry for the bad review Jersey Mike's but I felt it should be said.

review_info.review_text:
I can't believe I'm writing a review about a national chain sandwich shop, but good grief... 

I made an online order at 10:30am for a noon pickup, (2 sandwiches and a kids meal,) I showed up at noon, and they literally hadn't even started them?!  There was not a single customer in the shop and 4 employees, wondering around like chickens with their heads cut off? 

I told them to immediately get going on my sandwiches, and then once they finally began, it was llike watching paint dry. They took SO INSANELY LONG to make 3 small sandwiches. I've never seen anything like it!?  My 7 yr. old son could shuck a dozen oysters in less time...

Management needs to either start cracking the whip on these clowns or, just fire them and start over. 

Unreal!!!

Hubby and I stopped in here to get sandwiches a couple weekends ago.  First thing I noticed was that while no customers were in the store, the employee who was preparing things in the back was wearing his mask over one ear but not over his nose/mouth.  I could see this as I walked in.  The employee didn't notice us right away so I just watched.  Eventually they saw us and put their mask on properly and came over.  Our sandwiches were made correctly and quickly.  Jersey Mike's doesn't put very much meat on the default sandwich though so I recommend ordering double meat.  Everything was tasty and fresh.  Store was clean and easy to find just off the 101.  Down one star for questionable mask-wearing while no customers present.

First of all the two young teenage guys that were working we're very polite but when it comes to making sandwiches or food in general it didn't come out so good.
I got the number 55 the Big Kahuna chicken and I got the biggest size sandwich they had and then I also purchased a sandwich for later.
The Big Kahuna chicken was so nasty the chicken was overcooked, it was chewy and dry, when I opened the package to eat the sandwich it was soaking wet with what I'm assuming was the cheese? maybe??
Needless to say I ended up throwing it away that was an expensive sandwich to throw away but it was unedible.
I then tried to eat the sandwich that I had gotten  for later and it was soaking wet there was no reason why it should have been soaking wet.
I didn't get anything on it  to make it soaking wet no sauce  or any of that.
The bread was so soggy and it was only a matter of an hour prior to me opening  it that I had purchased it.
I had purchased a small sandwich for right then it was tuna I had asked how fresh the tuna was I wanted to see what it look like he grabbed the container ran back in the back and disappeared for a while then came back out and showed me the tuna and when I looked at it I could see he had made fresh tuna and put it on top of the existing I watched him put the fresher tuna on my sandwich but how fresh was that tuna I have no idea because it made me sick.
I know it was bad because I was nauseous for several hours before the tuna finally came back up.
My stomach didn't even digest the tuna which is a good sign that the food was bad when your stomach will not digest it, it knows better.
So I was only able to eat the little tiny sandwich which was the tuna and it tasted good at the time I ate it.
Later when I tried to eat my other sandwich before I was nauseous from the tuna, it was just disgusting I threw it away then I tried to eat my other sandwich that was supposed to be for later it was all soggy it was disgusting also.
I threw it away also and it was probably a good thing because if the tuna was bad God only knows how bad the other was needless to say I paid about $90 for all of our sandwiches and they didn't even come close to being as good as they looked when they were making them.
When they were making them they looked really good but this is one time looks can be very deceiving!
The only reason I'm writing this review is so that I hope nobody else gets sick first of all, and second of all they don't waste their money.
I had also left a 10% tip on our order.
All I have to say is eat cautiously if you eat here
If this was the first time I had ever had Jersey Mike's I would never go back.
Sorry for the bad review Jersey Mike's but I felt it should be said.

review_info.review_text:
I can't believe I'm writing a review about a national chain sandwich shop, but good grief... 

I made an online order at 10:30am for a noon pickup, (2 sandwiches and a kids meal,) I showed up at noon, and they literally hadn't even started them?!  There was not a single customer in the shop and 4 employees, wondering around like chickens with their heads cut off? 

I told them to immediately get going on my sandwiches, and then once they finally began, it was llike watching paint dry. They took SO INSANELY LONG to make 3 small sandwiches. I've never seen anything like it!?  My 7 yr. old son could shuck a dozen oysters in less time...

Management needs to either start cracking the whip on these clowns or, just fire them and start over. 

Unreal!!!

Hubby and I stopped in here to get sandwiches a couple weekends ago.  First thing I noticed was that while no customers were in the store, the employee who was preparing things in the back was wearing his mask over one ear but not over his nose/mouth.  I could see this as I walked in.  The employee didn't notice us right away so I just watched.  Eventually they saw us and put their mask on properly and came over.  Our sandwiches were made correctly and quickly.  Jersey Mike's doesn't put very much meat on the default sandwich though so I recommend ordering double meat.  Everything was tasty and fresh.  Store was clean and easy to find just off the 101.  Down one star for questionable mask-wearing while no customers present.

Needless to say I ended up throwing it away that was an expensive sandwich to throw away but it was unedible.
I then tried to eat the sandwich that I had gotten  for later and it was soaking wet there was no reason why it should have been soaking wet.
I didn't get anything on it  to make it soaking wet no sauce  or any of that.
The bread was so soggy and it was only a matter of an hour prior to me opening  it that I had purchased it.
I had purchased a small sandwich for right then it was tuna I had asked how fresh the tuna was I wanted to see what it look like he grabbed the container ran back in the back and disappeared for a while then came back out and showed me the tuna and when I looked at it I could see he had made fresh tuna and put it on top of the existing I watched him put the fresher tuna on my sandwich but how fresh was that tuna I have no idea because it made me sick.
I know it was bad because I was nauseous for several hours before the tuna finally came back up.
My stomach didn't even digest the tuna which is a good sign that the food was bad when your stomach will not digest it, it knows better.
So I was only able to eat the little tiny sandwich which was the tuna and it tasted good at the time I ate it.
Later when I tried to eat my other sandwich before I was nauseous from the tuna, it was just disgusting I threw it away then I tried to eat my other sandwich that was supposed to be for later it was all soggy it was disgusting also.
I threw it away also and it was probably a good thing because if the tuna was bad God only knows how bad the other was needless to say I paid about $90 for all of our sandwiches and they didn't even come close to being as good as they looked when they were making them.
When they were making them they looked really good but this is one time looks can be very deceiving!
The only reason I'm writing this review is so that I hope nobody else gets sick first of all, and second of all they don't waste their money.
I had also left a 10% tip on our order.
All I have to say is eat cautiously if you eat here
If this was the first time I had ever had Jersey Mike's I would never go back.
Sorry for the bad review Jersey Mike's but I felt it should be said.

response: The Manor Bar, located at 1759 S Jameson Ln in Montecito, California, is highly rated with 4.5 stars. The bar offers a range of services, including event planning and dining in a classy ambiance. It operates from 4 pm to 11 pm or midnight from Monday to Sunday, with free WiFi available for customers. However, it doesn't offer outdoor seating or takeout services, and it does not provide information about parking or music. Customers have praised the Manor Bar for its excellent cocktails, friendly and knowledgeable staff, and cozy atmosphere. The bar features dark wood paneling, intricate ceiling work, and a fireplace, giving it a relaxing and intimate feel. Despite some comments about dirty glasses on the bar top, customers seem to enjoy their time at the Manor Bar, with some even making plans for return visits.

source_info.name: The Manor Bar
source_info.categories: American (New), Nightlife, Hotels, Event Planning & Services, Restaurants, Hotels & Travel, Bars

review_info.review_text:
Matt B. and I spent Thanksgiving week at his dad's in Montecito, and on the Wednesday night in the cold and dark, we decided to walk to the Miramar for a nightcap. This wasn't our first time drinking at the hotel--we've been to the oceanfront bars a couple times, where we feel like we're getting the view/atmosphere/Rosewood experience for the relatively affordable price of two unreasonably expensive, mediocre cocktails. The Manor Bar doesn't come with views of the water, but it is an exceedingly lovely hotel bar and the cocktails are actually good.

We walked in around 10:00 the night before Thanksgiving, and the place was calm but not empty, which felt ideal. It was beautiful and cozy in a cigars-and-whiskey lounge kind of way, with dark wood paneling, intricate ceiling work, a fireplace, and leather and plush fabric furniture. We sat at the bar, which was very attractive, and ordered a round of drinks from a friendly, formally dressed bartender.

All the cocktails were named for books--a cute touch--and we got A Game of Thrones and a Catch-22. A Game of Thrones was a scotch drink with Glenmorangie 10 yr, Talisker 10 yr, lemon, citrus oleo saccharum, and egg white. An excellent cocktail, smoky and bright with a nice creamy froth on top. The Catch-22 was balanced and boozy, with Hennessy VSOP, Whistle Pig 10 yr, Dolin Rouge, and Benedictine.

We noticed a smoking cloche behind the bar and talked to the bartender about what it was used for, apparently a cocktail that wasn't on the current menu (but which he seemed perfectly able and ready to make). Maybe we'll try it next time we're at the Manor Bar. I suspect we'll make the walk over whenever we're in town.

A wonderful wood paneled clubby bar in the Rosewood Miramar this is a nearly perfect spot to enjoy fireside drinks and (at times) music. While we have come for years, I removed one star as the vast collection of dirty glasses on the bar top has somehow become a signature of the space. Also the food menu was better when the resort first opened with Caruso's Rigatoni being a beloved dish. Staff are kind, thoughtful if not all polished.

Best bartender super friendly and knowledgeable. I asked for a super complicated cocktail that was on the menu 3 years ago and made it in a jiffy. Love the live music and the vibe. Would come back any day

review_info.review_text:
Cute bakery with great assortment of bread.  We were hoping they had bagels and vegan cream cheese for our road trip but unfortunately they did not.  We did try the seed cookie which was amazing and very filling. Also loved the cinnamon rolls. 
They had an assortment of plant based cream cheeses that I would have loved to try. Unfortunately we were passing though and did not want to buy an entire container and large loaf.

We came here at the recommendation of Low Pigeon Coffee Roasters, looking for some bakery items to munch on with our coffees. Unfortunately, it was more bread than sweets, but we still walked away with some hygge buns and the most delicious foccocia bread. I wish we lived in SB just so we could appreciate their other breads because I couldn't justify getting a loaf only to have it sit for days before being able to enjoy it in our kitchen at home.

I got Half of a Seeded loaf. No flour. 
$15. Omg it was yum. Dense and complex. 
I don't live in the area but if I ever I'm in the area again I am definitely going to get the seeded loaf again.

review_info.review_text:
This place has become my go to place for nigiri. Whenever I am craving sushi I come here. This particular night, it was our first time eating in for dinner because our place had no electricity for 12 hours, we were hungry and needed some light. I usually order take out so it was different eating in. The rolls seemed a little bit bigger than when you order take out. review_info.review_text:
This place has become my go to place for nigiri. Whenever I am craving sushi I come here. This particular night, it was our first time eating in for dinner because our place had no electricity for 12 hours, we were hungry and needed some light. I usually order take out so it was different eating in. The rolls seemed a little bit bigger than when you order take out. The nigiri is usually consistent, occasionally when it's take out they sometimes give you more rice but the fish size is always the same. Some nigiris at other sushi places are tiny and cost double the price but at Sushi Teri the price is decent in comparison to the size of their nigiri. Which is the main reason I come here. 
We ordered quite a few things to try out other than our usual. We got the calamari, dynamite, four types of rolls, and uni, unagi and salmon nigiris. For the longest time I was looking for a decent dynamite dish and had no idea they served it here because it was never in the appetizer section, it was hidden as a meal. I really liked it for the fact that it's bigger with a lot of scallops and a few big mussels, the price itself was decent considering other places sell it for about the same price for the size of an appetizer. As for the calamari appetizer, it was a horrible fail, the batter was thin but it was not crispy, the initial bite felt like a dried jerky texture on the outside then after that initial bite you get the tenderness of the calamari. The uni nigiri was fresh as usual, the unagi and salmon was great! The four rolls we ordered were called Monkey roll, orange roll, broken heart roll and the real crab roll, we specifically got these roll because it didn't have any imitation crab on the inside. The Monkey roll was out favorite out of the four rolls. Our least favorite roll was the real crab roll, it was super disappointing because there was not enough real crab in it to taste it. I hope this place stays the same because I will continue coming here for their nigiris!

I've been eating here (as in all locations but mostly Goleta) for the past 20 years, and it never gets old. Sushi Terri is just the best and I don't understand why there are bad reviews. Sushi is always so good and tastes fresh. The miso soup broth is great. The staff is friendly and helpful. Always a quick meal too. I will eat at Sushi Terri for the rest of my life. Highly recommend.

Sushi Teri Goleta what an experience ! If you are looking for slow service and unpresentable rolls this is your place. Girlfriend and I were looking to grab some quick rolls and didn't feel like driving  down to Santa Barbara for the Sushi Teri on Bath St. So we decided to try out this location. I'd like to start off with the appetizers. Miso soup (with no seaweed!) had to be at least at room  temperature and spicy edamame was more
 of a garlic edamame For our rolls we had ordered one "Baked AF" and a "Broken Heart." The only "baked" part about the first roll was the tin foil. It had gotten stuck to our roll which eventually lead to the roll falling apart after we tried to grab a singular piece. I understood why they had named the second roll the "Broken Heart" because it had broke my heart when I saw how poorly this roll was presented. Noting back to the slow service, We were checked on once by our server and once she had heard about my experience another server attended to us one to drop off the check. So thank you Sushi Teri Goleta, will stick to supporting the location down town ! They never miss

The restaurant is open most days of the week, offering dinner service every day, and lunch service on Thursdays. It offers a range of amenities such as outdoor seating, free WiFi, valet parking, and restaurant reservations. The restaurant has an upscale ambiance and is well-suited for group gatherings. The restaurant has received a general rating of 4.0 stars. Customers praised the restaurant's patio dining, food quality, and service. The favorite dishes include an avocado toast with shrimp and a short rib salad. review_info.review_text: It's worth it to eat on their patio on the second floor.  I got the avo toast with shrimp and it was pretty good.  We wanted to eat here again the next day, but didn't realize they close at 3pm and open back up for dinner service.  Ugh.  So sad.  Need to eat here for dinner.  We got to come in because we stayed at the Four Seasons across the street.

I would rate this restaurant a solid 4.5 stars. My first experience i think happened to be an off night which can happen at any restaurant, but recently had a chance to dine here again and was impressed with the food and service. Obviously the setting is the biggest draw of the venue. It is situated perched above the beach with immaculate views of water, sand and cliffs. U can choose to sit outdoors or indoors, which also has views due to windows all around. There are space heaters outside so u can continue to enjoy if it gets chilly in the afternoon/evening. Regarding food, they have a nice mix of lighter and heavier options. We had a crab salad entree which was filled heavily with crab and really nicely seasoned, not heavy and full of filler like a lot of places. Our favorite dish was the short rib salad that had a korean style short rib next to a salad of baby romaine type lettuces and avocado. The short rib was perfectly seasoned and grilled, very impressive for a non-korean restaurant to be able to make it so tender and tasty. I was impressed with a mocktail i ordered that tasted just like a cocktail but without the alcohol. Usually mocktails are boring and uninventive but this was super tasty and thoughtful. Our server and wait staff were very helpful in food and drink recommendations and attentive throughout the meal. They surprised me with a ridiculously good piece of cake since we were celebrating a special occasion, which i thought was an extremely thoughtful gesture. The only reason id give 4.5 instead of 5 stars is the steep price, but given food quality and setting (really one of a kind in the world) u get what u pay for. Not a cheap quick meal but more of a special occassion location that u will truly enjoy ambiance, food and service.

I think u have to be fully confused to call the food here anything but really bad. The steak quality is similar to low end grocery store. My caesar salad was cheap grocery store romaine and wilted. The fries werent even good! Just so sad all around. Small portion, high prices. Giving two stars bc view and setting is amazing. I will never go back for the food!!

U can choose to sit outdoors or indoors, which also has views due to windows all around. There are space heaters outside so u can continue to enjoy if it gets chilly in the afternoon/evening. Regarding food, they have a nice mix of lighter and heavier options. We had a crab salad entree which was filled heavily with crab and really nicely seasoned, not heavy and full of filler like a lot of places. Our favorite dish was the short rib salad that had a korean style short rib next to a salad of baby romaine type lettuces and avocado. The short rib was perfectly seasoned and grilled, very impressive for a non-korean restaurant to be able to make it so tender and tasty. I was impressed with a mocktail i ordered that tasted just like a cocktail but without the alcohol. Usually mocktails are boring and uninventive but this was super tasty and thoughtful. Our server and wait staff were very helpful in food and drink recommendations and attentive throughout the meal. They surprised me with a ridiculously good piece of cake since we were celebrating a special occasion, which i thought was an extremely thoughtful gesture. The only reason id give 4.5 instead of 5 stars is the steep price, but given food quality and setting (really one of a kind in the world) u get what u pay for. Not a cheap quick meal but more of a special occassion location that u will truly enjoy ambiance, food and service.

I think u have to be fully confused to call the food here anything but really bad. The steak quality is similar to low end grocery store. My caesar salad was cheap grocery store romaine and wilted. The fries werent even good! Just so sad all around. Small portion, high prices. Giving two stars bc view and setting is amazing. I will never go back for the food!!

Finally, return the shrimp mixture to the skillet, add the cornstarch mixture, and bring the mixture to a boil. Cook and stir for 4-5 minutes or until the sauce is thickened, then sprinkle with coconut and serve with rice. Yield: 4 servings.

Mule deer have a black tip on their tail, which is noticeable against their white rump patch, while white-tailed deer do not have this black tip. Spicy Rice Pilaf Recipe

Ingredients:
- 2 cups chicken stock or vegetable stock
- 2 teaspoons olive oil
- 1 cup long-grain white or brown rice
- 1 teaspoon fennel seeds, crushed
- 1 teaspoon ground cardamon
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 1/4 cup slivered almonds
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper

Instructions:

1. Preheat oven to 300°F.
2. In a medium-size nonstick saucepan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add rice and cook until lightly browned, stirring occasionally.
3. Stir in the chicken stock or vegetable stock, fennel seed, ground cardamom, and ground cinnamon. Bring to a boil.
4. Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender and the liquid is gone, about 15-20 minutes for white rice and 35-40 minutes for brown rice.
5. Meanwhile, spread the slivered almonds on a baking sheet and toast them in the preheated oven for 10-12 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally.
6. Once the rice is cooked, discard the bay leaf from the saucepan and stir in the black pepper and almonds.
7. Serve hot.

1. Preheat the oven to 250F.
2. Place the steak on a rack over a baking sheet.
3. Rub the steak with 1 tablespoon of oil and season with salt and pepper.
4. Roast the steak in the center of the oven for about 20 minutes for medium-rare.
5. Remove the steak from the oven and heat oil in a medium skillet over high heat.
6. Add the steak to the skillet and sear until deep brown and crisp, about 3 minutes per side.
7. Hold the steak on its sides and cook the edges for 1 minute per side.
8. Remove the steak to a rack and let it rest for 10 minutes.

Birds do not have a diaphragm, so air is moved in and out of the respiratory system through pressure changes in the air sacs. The air sacs allow birds to ventilate their lungs by enabling a unidirectional flow of air through the lungs. This ensures that the air moving through the bird's lungs has a higher oxygen content, delivering more oxygen directly to the blood. Additionally, the air sacs play a role in creating negative pressure to draw air into the respiratory system. Lastly, birds have a larynx, but it is not used for sound production. Instead, the syrinx serves as the voice box for birds.

10. Leading by example, where leadership demonstrates a strong commitment to safety and sets the tone for the rest of the organization.

response:
Different diets and their benefits are varied depending on individual preferences and goals. For instance, the TLC (Therapeutic Lifestyle Changes) Diet focuses on consuming whole, nutrient-dense foods such as fruits, vegetables, whole grains, fish, and lean meats. This dietary pattern is beneficial for overall health and can help reduce the risk of heart disease. On the other hand, the Flexitarian Diet, a vegetarian approach, emphasizes replacing meat with plant-based protein sources like tofu, beans, lentils, peas, nuts, and eggs. This dietary style can aid in weight management and has environmental benefits.

Another option is the Slimfast Diet, a fast-paced weight loss program that involves consuming proprietary ready-made shakes, shake mixes, and meal bars while limiting daily caloric intake to 500 calories. This type of diet results in rapid weight loss but may not promote long-term success.

In addition, there are more specialized diets such as the alkaline diet, which advocates avoiding acidic foods with low pH levels, such as grains, dairy, meat, sugar, alcohol, caffeine, and fungi. Although this diet may have some health benefits, it is not supported by scientific evidence. Lastly, the blood type diet is based on the belief that an individual's diet should align with their blood type. However, this diet has been widely criticized due to lack of scientific backing and individual variations in blood type.

Overall, selecting the right diet depends on personal preferences, goals, and lifestyle factors. It is essential to consult a healthcare professional before starting any new diet regimen.

question: how to set up an email account on verizon

response:
To set up an email account on Verizon using Microsoft Outlook, follow these steps:

1. Open Microsoft Outlook and go to the "Change/View" menu.
2. Double-click on the email account you want to configure to access the settings screen.
3. Check the "My Server Requires Authentication" box.
4. Click through the Settings pop-up box into the "Log On Using" field and enter your Verizon email account name and password, as prompted.
5. Click on the "OK" button.
6. To set up the auto account setup process, open the "Add New Account" dialog box.
7. Configure the following settings in the "Email Account" section under "Auto Account Setup":
a. Type your full name in the "Your Name" box.
b. Type your e-mail address in the "Email Address" box.
c. Type the password that your ISP provided in the "Password" box.
d. Retype the password in the "Retype Password" box.
8. Click "Next" to begin the auto account setup process.
9. Outlook will then try to automatically configure your account.

Note: If your ISP requires the full email address to be entered into the "User Name" field, make sure to do so before proceeding with the auto account setup process.

response: Based on the passages, to cook sinigang na baboy, start by boiling sampalok in water until the shell shows cracks. In a pot, sauté garlic and onion then add tomatoes and let it simmer for 5 minutes. Add pork and fish sauce then add the rice wash. Bring to a boil then simmer for 15 minutes then add the gabi. response: To make ghee at home from milk, first keep the boiled milk in the refrigerator. After a few hours, skim the gathered cream on the top and collect it in a bowl over the course of a week or two. Churn the cream well in a mixer with the help of ice and water to make butter. Then, cook the refrigerated butter uncovered in a heavy saucepan over a medium heat. After a while, reduce the heat to a simmer and leave it to cool for half an hour. The butter will melt and separate into three layers - foam at the top, milk solids at the bottom, and clarified butter in between. Skim off the foam and pour the golden central layer through a strainer into a clean glass jar, leaving the milk solids at the bottom. Let the ghee cool for about 20 minutes and then strain it. Don't throw away the milk solids as they can be used in other recipes. Be careful not to overcook the ghee, as it will turn dark brown.

Step 1: Keep the boiled milk in the refrigerator for a week or two to allow the cream to rise to the top.

Step 3: Churn the cream well in a mixer with the help of ice and water to make butter.

response: To fry chicken in the oven, first preheat the oven to 425° F. In a shallow bowl, combine flour, paprika, salt, and pepper. Coat the chicken in the flour mixture. Alternatively, you can put the flour and seasonings in a bag, add the chicken pieces, and shake to coat. Put butter in a baking pan and place it in the preheated oven. Once the butter has melted, arrange the chicken in the pan in a single layer, skin side down. Bake for 30 minutes, then turn and bake for another 15 minutes, or until the chicken is done. Another method is to pour oil into a baking dish, add the chicken, sprinkle with paprika, and bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes. Turn the pieces over and bake for another 30 minutes. After removing from the oven, drain the chicken on paper towels.

question: how to fry chicken in the oven

response:
To fry chicken in the oven, you can follow these steps:

1. Preheat the oven to 425° F (220° C/Gas 7).
2. In a pie pan or a wide, shallow bowl, combine flour, paprika, salt, and pepper. You can also put the chicken in the flour mixture by shaking gently to coat.
3. Put butter in a shallow baking pan; place it in the preheated oven.
4. When the butter has melted, arrange the chicken in the baking pan in a single layer, skin side down.
5. Bake the chicken for 30 minutes, then turn and bake for another 15 minutes, or until chicken is tender and done.
6. If you prefer, you can pour oil into a 9x13 inch baking dish, add the chicken and sprinkle with paprika to taste. Then, bake the chicken for 30 minutes, turn pieces over and bake for another 30 minutes before removing from the oven and draining on paper towels.
7. Alternatively, you can place chicken in a roasting pan and season generously inside and out with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with onion powder and place 3 tablespoons margarine in the chicken cavity. Arrange dollops of the remaining margarine around the chicken's exterior, then bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for approximately 1 hour.

1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C/Gas 7).
2. In a pie pan or a wide, shallow bowl, mix together flour, paprika, salt, and pepper.
3. Coat the chicken pieces in the flour mixture, turning to ensure even coating.
4. Place butter in a shallow baking pan and put it in the preheated oven until melted.
5. Arrange the chicken pieces in a single layer, skin side down, in the baking pan.

1. Pour oil into a 9x13 inch baking dish.
2. Add the chicken to the dish and sprinkle with paprika to taste.
3. Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes, then turn the pieces over and bake for another 30 minutes.
